question: Which of the following statements best defines the term 'formula unit mass'?

options.text: The mass of an individual atom of an element
The sum of atomic masses of all atoms in a molecule
The sum of the atomic masses of the ions in an ionic compound as represented by its formula
The mass of one mole of a compound

solution:
The correct answer is __**The sum of the atomic masses of the ions in an ionic compound as represented by its formula**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **formula unit mass** of a substance is the **sum of the atomic masses** of all atoms in a **formula unit** of a compound.
 
• It is specifically used for substances whose constituent particles are **ions**. For example, in **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, the particles are **Na+** and **Cl-** ions rather than discrete molecules. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The calculation method is exactly the same as that for **molecular mass**; however, we use the term "formula unit" for those substances where the basic building blocks are ions.
 
• It represents the mass of one **formula unit** of an **ionic compound** relative to the mass of a **Carbon-12** atom.
